article.headline: Claude Code Adds Cron-Style Automation to Agentic Sessions
article.lede: Boris Cherny, creator and head of Claude Code at Anthropic, has shipped `/loop` — a slash command that turns an active Claude Code session into a lightweight recurring-task runner. The feature schedules prompts to fire at fixed or self-paced intervals for as long as the session remains live, letting a coding assistant keep watch on deployments, pull requests, and log files without further human input.
article.body:
The mechanics are deliberately spare. A developer types `/loop 5m check if the deployment finished` and **Claude** schedules the check as a repeating *cron* job, running every five minutes until cancelled. Three modes cover most needs: a fixed-interval prompt (the most explicit), a dynamic mode in which Claude chooses its own cadence based on what it observes, and a bare `/loop` with no arguments that activates a built-in maintenance prompt — scanning for unfinished work, unanswered pull-request review comments, and failed CI runs. The underlying machinery is three new tools — *CronCreate*, *CronList*, and *CronDelete* — that Claude calls on the user's behalf; developers who want direct control can supply precise cron expressions themselves.

The scheduling model borrows standard Unix cron conventions: five-field time expressions, deterministic jitter to prevent simultaneous session load on the API, and a hard 7-day expiry on recurring tasks. Tasks are **session-scoped** — they pause when the terminal session closes — but survive a restart if the session is resumed with `--resume` before the expiry lapses. A cap of 50 scheduled tasks per session and an environment variable (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1`) give administrators a ceiling and an off switch.

The use cases Cherny highlights skew toward overnight supervision: babysitting a pull request and auto-applying fixes when review comments arrive, watching deployment logs for errors, or generating a morning briefing from overnight code changes via a Slack *MCP* integration. For the bare `/loop` mode, the default prompt is conservative by design — irreversible actions proceed only if prior authorisation already exists in the session transcript. Developers can replace the default with a project-level `.claude/loop.md` file, capped at 25,000 bytes, whose edits take effect on the next iteration.

`/loop` occupies a deliberate middle tier in Anthropic's automation stack. For tasks that must run without an open laptop, the company offers cloud-hosted *Routines*, which execute on Anthropic's infrastructure and can be triggered on a schedule or by webhook. Desktop scheduled tasks cover local-file work that doesn't require an active session. `/loop` fills the gap between the two: local, ephemeral, contingent on a live session — suited to tasks a developer is supervising at arm's length rather than handing off entirely.

concepts.definition: A Unix utility that runs commands on a repeating schedule defined by a five-field time expression (minute, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week). Named after the Greek word for time, it is the standard mechanism for scheduled automation on Linux and macOS servers.

A resource or process that exists only for the duration of a single interactive session. A session-scoped scheduled task stops when the terminal session ends, as opposed to a persistent background service that survives restarts.

An open protocol introduced by Anthropic that lets AI assistants connect to external tools and data sources through a standardised interface. A Slack MCP integration, for instance, lets Claude read and post Slack messages as part of an automated workflow.

A Git feature that checks out a second working copy of a repository in a separate directory, without creating a new clone. Claude Code uses worktrees to run parallel agentic tasks — such as fixing a PR comment — in isolation from the main working directory.

Three internal Claude Code tools introduced alongside /loop that manage the underlying task schedule. CronCreate registers a new timed task with a cron expression and prompt; CronList shows all active tasks; CronDelete cancels one by its ID. Claude calls them automatically on /loop invocation, but they can also be addressed directly for precise control.

Anthropic's cloud-hosted automation layer for Claude Code, distinct from /loop. Routines execute on Anthropic infrastructure without requiring an open user session, can be triggered on a cron schedule or by webhook, and run in a fresh environment rather than the user's local filesystem.

A text shortcut beginning with a forward slash that invokes a specific skill or capability inside Claude Code. /loop, /review, and /compact are examples. Some are built into the runtime; others are user-defined skills loaded from the project or home directory.

article.fact_check: The announcement tweet states that /loop runs 'up to 3 days at a time.' The current official Claude Code documentation specifies a 7-day hard expiry on recurring tasks. The limit appears to have been extended after the initial release — the tweet was accurate at time of publication but is now out of date.
article.thread_summary: Cherny announces /loop in an opening tweet with two worked examples — overnight PR babysitting with auto-fix, and a daily morning Slack briefing — then follows with a 'Learn more' post linking to the official scheduled-tasks documentation.

poster_bcherny.blurb: Boris Cherny is a software engineer and author, best known for his book 'Programming TypeScript'. He writes about TypeScript, programming languages, and software engineering best practices. He has a modest following on X, where he shares technical insights and engages with the developer community.
